description: This topic covers the essential physical properties of solids and fluids, such as elasticity, surface tension, and viscosity. It is highly optimized for rapid revision and competitive exam preparation.

sections.title: Elasticity
sections.description: The property of a body by virtue of which it tends to regain its original size and shape after the applied deforming force is removed.

key_concepts.explanation: The characteristic of a material that opposes any external deforming force and returns the material to its original form once the force is removed.
The internal restoring force acting per unit cross-sectional area of a deformed body.
The ratio of the change in dimensions of a body to its original dimensions. It is a dimensionless quantity.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: Within the elastic limit, the stress developed in a body is directly proportional to the strain produced. (Stress ∝ Strain)
scientific_principles.application: Used in the manufacturing of spring balances and in structural engineering for material testing.
Crucial for selecting appropriate materials for the construction of bridges and buildings.

important_facts.fact: Steel is more elastic than rubber because the Young's modulus of steel is significantly higher.
Quartz and phosphor bronze are considered nearly perfectly elastic bodies, whereas wet clay is perfectly plastic.

sections.title: Surface Tension
sections.description: The property of the free surface of a liquid at rest to behave like a stretched elastic membrane and tend to contract to occupy minimum surface area.

key_concepts.explanation: The force of attraction between molecules of the same substance. It is maximum in solids.
The force of attraction between molecules of different substances.
The phenomenon of the rise or fall of a liquid inside a capillary tube.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The height of liquid in a capillary tube h = 2Tcosθ / rρg, where T is surface tension and r is the radius of the tube.
scientific_principles.application: Explains the ascent of sap in plants and the rise of oil in the wick of a lantern.

key_associations.item: Adding detergent or soap to water
key_associations.extra_info: Lowers surface tension so water penetrates fabric pores easily, leading to cleaner clothes.
Hot soup tastes better because its lower surface tension allows it to spread over a larger area of the tongue.

important_facts.fact: Raindrops and soap bubbles acquire a spherical shape strictly due to surface tension.
Spraying kerosene oil on stagnant water lowers its surface tension, causing mosquito larvae to sink and drown.

sections.title: Viscosity
sections.description: The internal property of a fluid that offers resistance to the relative motion between its adjacent layers.

key_concepts.explanation: The fluid friction that prevents liquids and gases from flowing freely.
The maximum constant velocity acquired by a freely falling body moving through a viscous medium.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: F = 6πηrv (where η is the coefficient of viscosity, r is the radius, and v is the velocity).
scientific_principles.application: Explains the safe, slow descent of a parachute and the formation of clouds.

important_facts.fact: As temperature increases, the viscosity of liquids decreases, but the viscosity of gases increases.
Honey and glycerin have a much higher viscosity compared to water.
The viscosity of an ideal, non-viscous fluid is absolute zero.

sections.title: Fluid Mechanics and Pressure
sections.description: The study of the behavior of fluids at rest and in motion, including the pressure exerted by them.

key_concepts.explanation: The upward force exerted by a fluid on an object that is partially or completely immersed in it.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: An external pressure applied to any part of an enclosed fluid is transmitted equally in all directions without undiminished magnitude.
scientific_principles.application: The working principle behind hydraulic lifts, hydraulic brakes, and hydraulic presses.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: The apparent loss of weight of an object immersed in a fluid is equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
scientific_principles.application: Used in designing submarines and ships, and for determining the relative density of solid substances.

scientific_principles.formula_or_statement: For the streamline flow of an incompressible and non-viscous fluid, the total energy (Pressure + Kinetic + Potential energy) per unit volume remains constant.
scientific_principles.application: Explains aerodynamic lift of airplanes, the operation of a venturimeter, and the Magnus effect (swing of a spinning cricket ball).

sections.title: Important Units and Measuring Instruments
sections.description: Crucial SI units and scientific instruments used to measure the properties of matter and fluids.

key_associations.extra_info: Adding impurities to water changes its surface tension.
The CGS unit is Poise (1 Poiseuille = 10 Poise).
Instrument used to measure the density of liquids.
A specialized hydrometer based on Archimedes' principle.
